answers.q1_what_did_you_play: I played Rummage first, spending 3 Sparks and 1 energy to draw 3 cards. With the Spark bank gone, Rapid Fire reverted to its printed cost of 2, so I played it next for 2 energy, dealing 16 damage to Seapunk. I finished with Duck and Cover for 1 energy, gaining 5 Block before Seapunk’s telegraphed 11 damage attack.
answers.q2_other_line_considered: I seriously considered playing Rapid Fire first at its Spark-discounted cost of 0, then Duck and Cover for 1 energy. That line would deal the same 16 damage and gain the same 5 Block, but it would leave 3 energy unused and would not draw the 3 cards that Rummage provides. I also considered skipping Duck and Cover after Rummage in order to spend the remaining energy on a drawn card, but the drawn card’s exact printed title and effect were not known from the page, so I did not commit to that line.
answers.q3_what_it_gave_up: The chosen line gave up the chance to use the remaining energy on a card drawn by Rummage. It also gave up the immediate Spark discount on Rapid Fire, paying 2 energy instead of 0. In exchange, it gained 3 cards for later and kept the same immediate damage and Block as the simpler Rapid Fire plus Duck and Cover line.
answers.q4_different_intent: No. A different telegraphed intent would not have changed this line. If Seapunk had telegraphed a weaker attack, Duck and Cover would have been less valuable, but Rummage plus Rapid Fire would still be the strongest known immediate-damage line that does not depend on naming an unknown drawn card. If Seapunk had telegraphed a stronger attack, Duck and Cover would have been even more valuable, not less. The core tradeoff was between drawing with Rummage and using the Spark discount on Rapid Fire, and the declared 11 damage made keeping Duck and Cover reasonable.
